g.text: The pixel-sampled ground truth itself resolves only up to 9-4 (G9-E5 lines are 1.08 px wide) — a sampling ceiling of the simulation grid, not a measured resolution.

text.style: fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: 0.80 µm; LRFC-style HDR 16 bit: 9-4, FRC 0.57 µm; published ML-HDR 16 bit: 8-2, FRC 1.39 µm; ML + mask 16 bit: 9-4, FRC 0.57 µm. LRFC-style HDR 16 bit and ML + mask 16 bit reach the simulation ceiling: 9-4 and FRC at Nyquist (0.571 µm).

text.style: fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: Reconstruction: our pure-NumPy mPIE (250 iterations), not the PtyLab engine of the recorded experiment; PtyLab defaults except alpha_probe = 1.0, plus probe centre-of-mass stabilisation. Smallest resolved element and FRC — single 16 bit: 9-1, FRC

text.style: fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: GROUND TRUTH, van Heel half-bit threshold; labels give dx / cutoff. A crossing at the first ring ≥ 0.05 Nyquist (≥ 9.88 µm) means no resolution (a floor) and is not drawn as a cutoff. Images, profiles and FRC curves are single runs (seed 0).

text.style: fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: (e) Reconstructed AMPLITUDE |O| after global alignment (the paper labels its axis 'intensity'); thin gray = ideal USAF square wave (1.0 background / 0.15 bars) from the geometry; the single exposure at 16 bit is shown for reference. (f) FRC against the

text.style: fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: 160–163); dashed cyan box = smallest element resolved together with all coarser ones (resolution_summary.json).
